name: Paul Keating
description: Australian prime minister associated with economic liberalisation, compulsory superannuation and Indigenous reconciliation.
scope: Public positions and conduct during the specified period; this represents the individual rather than all party members or citizens.

axes.brief: Electoral and constitutional government framed his republican proposals.
axes.counter: His proposed republic selected a president through Parliament rather than a popular presidential vote.

axes.brief: Civil institutions coexisted with mandatory immigration detention and regulated personal conduct.
axes.counter: Free expression was qualified by anti-discrimination protections.

axes.brief: Multicultural nationhood and Indigenous reconciliation were explicit priorities.
axes.counter: Recognition of pluralism still included democratic common obligations.

axes.brief: Multicultural selection coexisted with managed entry and mandatory detention.
axes.counter: Cultural diversity does not prove support for irregular migrants remaining without conditions.

axes.brief: Regional engagement and diplomacy coexisted with alliance and defence commitments.
axes.counter: Later AUKUS criticism is outside this premiership.

axes.brief: Asian engagement and APEC cooperation accompanied an independent Australian identity.
axes.counter: Sovereign currency and national decision-making remained.

axes.brief: Qantas and Commonwealth Bank privatisation coexisted with public health and other public assets.
axes.counter: Private provision was not an instruction to privatise the ABC or every strategic network.

axes.brief: Tariff reduction and competitiveness favoured open trade.
axes.counter: Industry adjustment and negotiated agreements qualify unrestricted unilateral abolition.

axes.brief: Competition and enterprise bargaining expanded while minimum standards and social protections remained.
axes.counter: Government development support prevents a pure laissez-faire description.

axes.brief: Targeted family support and retirement reform accompanied market-oriented growth.
axes.counter: Compulsory private superannuation saving differs from tax-funded equalisation.

axes.brief: Civil government and republican institutions were separate from his personal Catholic faith.
axes.counter: Religious schools, holidays and exemptions remained.

axes.brief: Reconciliation and social inclusion marked his premiership.
axes.counter: Earlier opposition to homosexual decriminalisation and conventional family views complicate extrapolation.

axes.brief: Productivity and development were priorities alongside environmental safeguards.
axes.counter: Modern enhancement policies remain undocumented analogies.

axes.brief: National economic and Indigenous-rights frameworks coexisted with federation.
axes.counter: Regional tax and administrative rights did not extend to unilateral secession.

reasons.4: The scoped national institutions retained constitutional states with their own governmental constitutions. Federal programme supremacy does not remove that protected institutional role.
reasons.5: State and local police retained ordinary jurisdiction. National security coordination does not establish support for replacing them with a single national police authority.

axes.brief: His national story explained inequality through dispossession and discrimination.
axes.counter: That historical account does not settle genetics in every psychological domain.
axes.gap: The causal responses are provisional, especially temperament and attention; Indigenous reconciliation is not treated as proof of a biological theory.
